policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'their beauty' renders the noun as 'form/figure', a sense readers take from either the qere וצורם (as צוּרָה, form) or the ketiv וצירם (ציר, image/form); no ASV wording or italic supply favours one spelling. The only note, 'Or, form', is classed alternative_rendering and concerns English wording, not the reading. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
